result_json.summary: Phase 1 delivers pure, well-factored governance types, a fingerprint, and a closure/debt validator; tests, typecheck, and lint pass and the dependency boundary is clean. Three P1 policy defects reject legitimate verdicts in enforced mode: a fingerprint change on partially addressed findings, adjacent human_required debt with a credit claim, and debt-eligibility drift from plan 208. New closure blockers also skip the identity-field checks. Two items need human policy decisions before Phase 3/4 consume the validator.

items.title: A changed fingerprint on a remaining prior finding is rejected, which conflicts with partially_addressed
items.reason: closure.ts:509-522 emits PRIOR_FINDING_FINGERPRINT_CHANGED whenever the title, failure, or lowestCostCorrection of a still-open or partially-addressed item differs from the persisted identity, and enforced mode rejects the verdict. A partially addressed finding naturally narrows its remaining correction (probe confirmed). The plan treats a changed fingerprint as changed evidence, not as a rejection. Someone must choose: make it informational (severity or record the new fingerprint), or keep identity fields stable via a separate remaining-work field. This affects the Phase 3 protocol and Phase 7 templates.

items.title: Adjacent human_required debt items with a creditClaim are rejected via DEBT_COUPLING_INELIGIBLE
items.reason: The plan permits adjacent debt in items[] with action human_required (no credit). validateDebtPolicy also runs assessDebtEligibility, which returns non_intrinsic and emits DEBT_COUPLING_INELIGIBLE, so enforced mode rejects the verdict (probe confirmed). Only the single adjacent/unrelated rule should produce coupling violations; non-intrinsic eligibility should mean zero credit. Add a test that adjacent + human_required + claim is valid.

items.title: Debt eligibility recomputes plan-208 rules and diverges from eligibleN
items.reason: The plan says to reuse advisory evidence and not recalculate eligibility. assessDebtEligibility requires the reviewer to self-assess its own reviewer-authored claim, which plan-208 eligibleN does not require. Its not_simpler rule compares architectureDelta with minimalAlternativeArchitectureDelta instead of plan 208 architectureDelta<0. It rejects every ineligible claim instead of withholding credit. It adds an undocumented /^phase/ targetPhase format. Probes showed plan-208-credited claims rejected in both directions. Someone must decide which source of truth governs reviewer-authored claims and whether ineligibility rejects or only withholds credit.

items.title: New closure-round blockers are not required to carry failure, lowestCostCorrection, or deltas, so they cannot be fingerprinted
items.reason: validateInitialItem runs only for initial reviews. A closure critical-safety, introduced, or re-raise item without failure or lowestCostCorrection validates (probe: valid true), but fingerprintItem returns null, so Phase 2 cannot persist its FindingIdentity or match deferrals. Apply the validateInitialItem field and material-failure checks to every new closure item not in requiredIds, and add tests.

items.title: Critical-safety evidence regex also matches the failure text
items.reason: closure.ts:259-264 tests failure + lateDiscoveryEvidence together, so a safety keyword in failure satisfies the concrete-evidence requirement even when lateDiscoveryEvidence is contentless. Test lateDiscoveryEvidence alone.

items.title: Add tests for untested diagnostic codes and stale-decision variants
items.reason: No tests cover PRIOR_FINDING_FINGERPRINT_CHANGED, PRIOR_FINDING_ITEM_MISSING/UNEXPECTED, INTRODUCED_AND_CRITICAL_CONFLICT, INTRODUCED_HUNK_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, CRITICAL_SAFETY_SCOPE_INVALID, or PRIOR_DECISION_NEW_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED, and none cover superseded, inactive, or non-risk decisions. The debt tests use order-dependent [0] assertions. Follow the existing fixture pattern.

items.title: isRiskDecision accepts invented defer/accept_risk aliases
items.reason: The plan defines only defer_accept_risk as the risk choice. Restrict isRiskDecision to it, and type ReviewDecision.choice when Phase 2 adds the payload union.

result_json.guidance: Follow the approved plan literally: treat a same-ID fingerprint change as visible changed evidence rather than an automatic closure rejection; preserve stable-ID accounting. Reuse plan-208 debt evidence and eligibleN semantics, enforcing only plan-209 complete-evidence, intrinsic-coupling, valid-target, and genuinely-simpler-After guardrails. Address all reviewer items P1.1-P2.3 and add the requested tests.

items.title: P1.1 deriveOpenGate reopens an older snapshot gate when the latest snapshot has no causes
items.reason: store.ts filters snapshots to non-empty effectiveGateCauses before .at(-1), so a newer cause-free snapshot falls back to an older unresolved gate (probe: snap1 [over_effective] + snap2 [] returns snap1 gate open). Use the latest decodable snapshot and return null when it has no causes; add regression test.

items.title: P2.1 resolveGate loser lookup wrong for step-key collisions and corrections
items.reason: Human step key depends only on phase/iteration; a step-key-only collision (e.g. successor gate at same iteration) throws REVIEW_GATE_ALREADY_RESOLVED spuriously, and correction conflicts look up governanceDecisionKey instead of governanceCorrectionKey. Look up the written key, raise a distinct error for step-key collisions, add tests.

items.title: P2.2 rebuildRecordsIndex appends git-committed lines into a caller-supplied authoritative RecordStore
items.reason: projectionStore = opts.recordStore ?? memory store, then putRun/append into it; a caller passing the working-tree store would mutate authoritative JSONL during index rebuild. Always project via a fresh memory store or read without mutating.

items.title: P2.3 Live deriveOpenGate throws on malformed gate decision while reindex treats it as unresolved
items.reason: decodeReviewDecisionPayload throws inside deriveOpenGate; reindex excludes the decision. Plan requires malformed governance be diagnosed, not fatal, and live/rebuild parity. Catch, treat as unresolved, add test.

items.title: P2.4 Write-through governance index upserts are private and unused
items.reason: Plan 2.3 requires write-through upserts; upsertDecision/upsertGate are module-private with no live caller, so projections only populate via records index rebuild. Export a per-run projection helper for the Phase 5 handler.

items.title: P2.5 Annotate over-claimed Phase 2 checkboxes with the completing phase
items.reason: Checkboxes for record-time effective-cause computation (Phase 6.1), prompt projection/repair (Phase 5), and ReviewBudgetCommandContext facade are marked done but only schema/seams exist; routeForChoice human_gate vs deriveOpenGate null for increase_budget is an interim gap pending Phase 4. Annotate for audit accuracy.

items.title: P2.6 Add stale-fold, supersession, and rebuild governing-state parity tests
items.reason: The stale audit-only fold test never includes a stale decision; supersedesDecisionId folding is untested; rebuild test compares index rows but not governing state parity as the plan requires.

items.title: P2.7 review_gate_index.record_seq uses a cross-run cumulative counter
items.reason: seq + gateCount accumulates across runs and has no stable meaning; use budget line seq plus chain depth.
